The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the accused/ applicant in Case Crime No.129 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 of I.P.C. & 5j(ii)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Sindhoura,
District Varanasi with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

Heard Shri Brij Kishore Pandey & Shri Ajay Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the accused/applicant, Shri Shambhavi Nandan, learned counsel for the complainant, Shri Rabindra Kumar Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the accused applicant submitted that the accused applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The victim is a contesting party.
She willingly went with the accused applicant and they both got married.

He further submitted that the victim has not supported the prosecution version in her statements recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. As Deepak Rajbhar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39829272/

sentences.text: per the ossification test report, the age of victim has been found between 18 to 19 years.

He further submitted that the accused applicant is languishing in jail since 11.07.2022 and he is having no criminal history as stated in para 3 of the supplementary affidavit filed in support of the bail application.
Hence the applicant should be enlarged on bail.
Learned counsel for the informant opposed the bail application of the accused applicant and submitted that the victim is a minor girl and her consent being minor, has no meaning in the eyes of law.
Learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State opposed the bail application of the accused/applicant but could not dispute the aforementioned facts.
Considered the rival submissions made by the parties' counsel and perused the material available on record.
It transpires from the record that the victim has not supported the prosecution case in her statement recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C.
As per the ossification report test, her age has been found between 18 to 19 years.
Considering all the fact and circumstances of the case as mentioned above, without commenting on merits, it appears just to enlarge the accused applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application filed on behalf of applicant is allowed.

Let the applicant Deepak Rajbhar involved in Case Crime No.129 of 2022 (supra) be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions;
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against his under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against his, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
